answer: Agents stake a jade token deposit bound to a hardware-backed cipher key, and each identity must maintain a unique thread of attested work history signed across epochs. Creating a fake identity costs a full deposit plus the compute to forge a valid thread, which peers reject because the cipher signature chain fails verification. Duplicating identities multiplies these sunk costs, making sybil swarms economically irrational when honest participation yields higher returns.
